title: Expense/Record Tracker Using Collections
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of expense/record tracker using collections.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: A record tracker stores multiple entries in a collection and supports creating, listing, summarizing, searching, and removing records. Each entry should have a consistent shape and validation rules. A collection is useful for handling a group of records; data persistence can be added later and should be clearly distinguished from in-memory storage.
understand.whyItMatters: This project connects collection structures, data fields, iteration, functions, validation, and basic aggregation.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
A record tracker stores multiple entries in a collection and supports creating, listing, summarizing, searching, and removing records. Each entry should have a consistent shape and validation rules. A collection is useful for handling a group of records; data persistence can be added later and should be clearly distinguished from in-memory storage.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Build an in-memory tracker for records with id, description, category, and amount. Add entries, list them, compute totals, and filter by category. Validate empty descriptions and negative amounts according to your chosen rules.
steps: Build an in-memory tracker for records with id, description, category, and amount. Add entries, list them, compute totals, and filter by category. Validate empty descriptions and negative amounts according to your chosen rules.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Extend the tracker with update/delete, date filtering, summary totals, unique IDs, and a test plan. Clearly state whether records persist after the program exits; do not imply storage if none is implemented.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
